content.text: {"answer": 2, "reduction": 2, "lower_bound": 2, "upper_bound": 2, "lower_bound_mechanism": "finiteness of minimal elements via greedy 'killing property' (K/K'): descent forcing pi(t*_w) <= a_1*w, pigeonhole on prime-sets of product <= a_1, compactness (no infinite minimal transversal) + peeling", "upper_bound_mechanism": "L = lcm of finitely many squarefree minimal elements; membership in S_inf invariant under m -> m+L for all m; T = #(S_inf ∩ [a_1, a_1+L)), block bijection gives a_{n+T}=a_n+L for all n>=1", "wrong_answer_stated": false, "notes": "Step 1 gives the full membership characterization; Step 2 gives global (not eventual) periodicity from n=1 with explicit T,L. Finiteness is proved abstractly (intersecting antichain, finite self-duality, K'-descent, compactness, peeling) rather than by direct large-prime erasure, but is written out for all cases and appears sound. Minor: trivial P_0=∅ edge case, one LaTeX typo."}
